title: SLO attribution and weighted error budgeting for multi-variant model endpoints
creator: Nadia Patel
description: Define a repeatable SLI/SLO attribution model and a weighted error-budget policy for endpoints that serve multiple model variants (e.g., model A, model B, fallback light models). The goal is to: 1) attribute user-visible errors and latency to the correct model variant and route, 2) compute a weighted error budget that accounts for variant traffic share and business criticality, and 3) derive automated circuit-breaker and load-shedding triggers driven by budget burn rates and regional capacity constraints. Deliverables: SLI definitions, per-variant weights and rationale, error-budget calculation examples, circuit-breaker burn-rate thresholds, and a short implementation plan (metrics, alerts, dashboarding, rollout steps).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI definitions for success/failure and latency percentiles for model endpoints (per-variant and aggregated)
A documented formula for weighted error budgets with examples for common traffic mixes (A:70%, B:20%, fallback:10%)
Clear mapping from error-budget burn rates to automated actions: throttle, isolate variant, regional failover, and aggressive load shedding
Prometheus/metric names and tags for emitting variant attribution (model_name, variant_tag, region, route)
Dashboard mock in Grafana showing burn rate, budget remaining, per-variant SLI, and active circuit breakers
Implementation plan with PR owners, required infra work, and a canary rollout path that respects customer-affecting thresholds
notes: Motivation: current SLOs are endpoint-wide and poorly attribute incidents when a single variant misbehaves; this causes noisy on-call paging and inefficient rollbacks.
We will treat variant weight as a combination of observed traffic fraction and business criticality multiplier (0.0-2.0). Example: weight_variant = traffic_fraction * criticality_multiplier.
Error types to include in budget: 5xx responses upstream from runtime, model runtime OOMs, decoding errors, and >P99 latency depending on SLOs. Non-actionable client errors (4xx) excluded by default.

Burn-rate-driven actions (suggested): burn_rate > 2x for 10m => open soft circuit breaker for variant; burn_rate > 4x for 5m => hard isolate variant and route to fallback; cross-region burn triggers regional failover policy.
Circuit breaker state machine: CLOSED -> SOFT_OPEN (observability + rate limit) -> OPEN (isolate variant) -> HALFWAY (test with canary 1%) -> CLOSED. Each transition emits an event to tracing bus.
Regional considerations: compute error budgets per-region and globally. Global failover only when region-level budget depleted and cross-region capacity available per routing policy.
Dashboard panels: per-variant SLI trend, rolling burn-rate heatmap, active CB list, per-region budget stack chart, and recent variant rollouts linked to PRs.

Implementation rough steps: 1) instrument variant attribution in runtime (tags), 2) add metrics and burn-rate computation in alerting pipeline, 3) build CB controller that subscribes to burn-rate signals, 4) create dashboards and runbook, 5) canary rollout on low-traffic customer to validate graceful degradation.
Rollout risk: inaccurate variant weights can under/overreact; plan includes a 2-week observation window with manual tuning before enabling automated hard-isolate actions.
Estimated infra work: small runtime tag propagation (ENG), burn-rate computation in alerting service (SRE), CB controller in control plane (ENG).
